clue.text: Have to follow safety test for record label

indicators.note: the verb comes after the test in the answer, so it follows it

parts.note: the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for vehicles
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: An instruction to put 'have' after a safety test to get the name of a record label.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness check for cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Motown is the famous Detroit record company behind the Supremes and Stevie Wonder.

clue.text: Singer put on that fellow's clothing article

indicators.note: the man wraps around the word, clothing it

parts.note: that fellow is a man
to don a garment is to put it on
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A singer putting on an item of clothing belonging to some man.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna is the American pop star known as the Queen of Pop.

clue.text: Satisfied after raising sleuth's rates

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a word turns it upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a need that is met is satisfied
PI is a private investigator, a sleuth; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A detective is pleased after his fees go up.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the musical speeds of pieces, plural of tempo, so rates of performance.

clue.text: Rain-hit event wasn't in entertaining hotel

indicators.note: the phrase holds the hotel inside, as a host entertains a guest

parts.note: someone not in was out
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An event spoiled by rain at which someone was absent from the hotel's festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: A washout is an event ruined by rain, and by extension any complete failure.

clue.text: Barker's call for a cigarette

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the shout of a fairground barker drawing in customers

explanation.walkthrough: A barker is a fairground or circus tout; 'Barker' might suggest a dog, but it is the showman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-made smoke rolled from loose tobacco is called by this name, as is a showman's cry inviting the crowd.

clue.text: Men on island around northern British Isles

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so first

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: the island word goes around the northern letter

parts.note: a key is a low island or reef, as in Florida

explanation.surface: Soldiers stationed on an island in the north of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is a stock military term for enlisted men.
explanation.definitionFit: Orkney is the archipelago off northern Scotland, part of the British Isles.

clue.text: See no good PM save on underwear

parts.note: lo is an old word for see!

indicators.note: save means except, so the following word is left out

parts.note: Boris Johnson was UK prime minister
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch an inept prime minister cut costs on something.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson was Britain's prime minister from 2019 to 2022; 'save on' looks like economising but removes ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Long johns are warm full-length underpants worn in cold weather.

clue.text: Star is to divide opinion after striking finale

indicators.note: the finale is the last letter, which is struck out

parts.note: to polarise is to divide opinion sharply

explanation.surface: A star divides critics after a controversial final performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris is the North Star, the bright star nearly above the Earth's north pole.

clue.text: Seizing end piece, conceited revellers may get a punch here

definitions.text: revellers may get a punch here

indicators.note: the conceited word grabs the other piece and holds it inside

parts.note: cocky means conceited
a tail is an end
a part is a piece

explanation.surface: Arrogant partygoers might get punched after grabbing a final bit of food.
explanation.walkthrough: The punch is not a blow but the bowl of mixed drink served at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Guests at a drinks gathering are often served punch, a mixed drink from a bowl.

clue.text: First progenitor?

parts.note: A is the first letter, as in A1 or A for first class
a dam is the mother of an animal, its progenitor

explanation.surface: A question asking who was the very first ancestor of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: A for 'first' plus DAM, a parent of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man is the forefather of the whole human race.

clue.text: Drinking wine, croon covers of Lead Belly in a bad way

indicators.note: the singing word takes the wine inside it as if drinking it down

parts.note: to croon is to sing
hock is a German white wine

indicators.note: the covers of a phrase are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: the first and last letters of Lead Belly

explanation.surface: Someone sipping wine while crooning a blues number covers Lead Belly badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is a British name for Rhine wine. Lead Belly was the American blues singer, which makes 'covers' look like cover versions.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means dreadfully or appallingly, which is to say badly.

clue.text: During archaeological work, nothing's in the shade

parts.note: in can mean during, as in 'in the war'
an excavation is a dig
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: At an excavation, nothing is happening because everyone is resting in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue colour, and a colour is a shade.

clue.text: Unthinking king — born idiot!

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
née marks a maiden name: born
a jerk is an idiot

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a monarch who is a natural fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex response made without reflection is automatic, done without thinking.

clue.text: He's on the end of a cross termagant's raving

definitions.text: He's on the end of a cross

indicators.note: the letters are made to rave wildly, so they are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of termagant; the possessive s is a link joining the anagram to its indicator

explanation.surface: A man suffers at the receiving end of a furious shrew's ranting.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a cross is a ball played from the wing into the box; the striker it is aimed at is the one in question. The apostrophe s does not enter the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: In football this is the tall striker whom wingers aim their crosses at in the penalty area.

clue.text: Art of songwriting shown by Elgar furiously penning dance music

indicators.note: the jumbled name encloses the music, as a pen holds animals
working furiously, the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the letters of Elgar
funk is a style of dance music

explanation.surface: The composer Elgar shows his songwriting skill by writing frenzied dance music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is a name, not a skill: Art Garfunkel of Simon and Garfunkel.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Garfunkel sang in the folk duo Simon and Garfunkel, a songwriting partnership.

clue.text: European leaves America just like that

indicators.note: the European departs, so that letter is removed

parts.note: America is the US, here with its article: the US

explanation.surface: A European walks out on America without warning, just like that.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in this manner, so, like that.

clue.text: Material that floats in either end of creek

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
either end of the word creek, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outer letters of creek
either goes with or, so it gives OR

explanation.surface: Something buoyant drifting at one end or other of a creek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either' gives OR, which sits between the two ends of 'creek'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bark of the cork oak is light and buoyant, used for fishing floats and bottle stoppers.

clue.text: Nibble away at my caviar? Penny tucks into it

parts.note: cor! is an exclamation like my!

indicators.note: the penny goes into the fish eggs

parts.note: caviar is roe, fish eggs
d is the old abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: An exclamation at caviar, with someone called Penny eating it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is an exclamation of surprise, as is the British 'cor'; d stands for the old penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrode is to wear away gradually, as rust eats into metal.

clue.text: Distressed pangolins' sound heard in church

indicators.note: upset or damaged, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of pangolins

explanation.surface: Anxious pangolins making a noise that is heard in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainchant is the unaccompanied singing of medieval liturgy, music performed in services.

clue.text: Wrong marks twice taken in by person setting exam

indicators.note: the marks are held inside the following words

parts.note: the setter calls themselves I
an oral is a spoken exam
M is mark, the old German currency
twice means the mark letter is given a second time

explanation.surface: A dishonest examiner accepts wrong answers twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of the puzzle is 'I'; the mark is the old German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoral means morally bad, contrary to accepted ethics.

clue.text: Moving more freely, medic dives into one river, then another

indicators.note: the medic plunges into the river

parts.note: the Nile is a river
MB is a medical degree, so a doctor
another river: R is short for river

explanation.surface: A doctor plunges into one river and then another.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimble means agile and quick on the feet, so its comparative means moving with more freedom.

clue.text: About to follow football team — it's put out on field

indicators.note: the about word comes after the team

parts.note: Man U is Manchester United
re means about

explanation.surface: A fan about to follow a football team onto the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Man U is the nickname of Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers spread dung over farmland as fertiliser.

clue.text: Family member you heard laugh creates uproar

parts.note: bro is short for brother

indicators.note: the word is spoken aloud, so its sound gives a letter

parts.note: the word you, which is said like the letter U
ha-ha is a laugh

explanation.surface: A sibling's laughter at your expense leads to a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or commotion over something.

clue.text: Foul air current inhaled by maternal grandmother

indicators.note: the current is breathed in, so it goes inside the grandmother

parts.note: a maternal grandmother is one's ma's ma
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An old lady breathes in a current of polluted air.
explanation.walkthrough: Your maternal grandmother is your mother's mother, MA'S MA run together, and I goes after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious vapour, once believed to carry disease.

clue.text: At intervals, gamely holding jacket for Bob Monkhouse?

indicators.note: the alternate letters hold the other letters inside
taking letters at intervals means every other letter

parts.note: alternate letters of gamely

indicators.note: a jacket is the outer layer, here the first and last letters

parts.note: the outer letters of Bob

explanation.surface: Gamely wearing a jacket that once belonged to the comedian Bob Monkhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Monkhouse was a British comedian; the name splits, and Monkhouse is read as a house for monks.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks live in a monastery church and buildings, so it is literally a monk house.

clue.text: Break into mostly crazy book full of it

indicators.note: the break goes into the other piece
most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: bonkers means crazy
to bust is to break

explanation.surface: Someone breaks into a book that is mostly mad and full of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the slang for sex, so the definition is a book full of sex scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonkbuster is a racy popular novel crammed with sex, which is what 'it' means.

clue.text: Fare from India, not heading for Thai island

indicators.note: the heading is not there, so it is taken out

parts.note: a balti is a curry dish from the Indian subcontinent

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Thai

explanation.surface: Indian food, rather than the Thai variety, on an island holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thai island' reads as one phrase, but Thai only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Shelter fenced off by a German lady

indicators.note: the shelter is enclosed by the German word, as by a fence

parts.note: ein is German for a
lee is the shelter on the side away from the wind

explanation.surface: A German woman behind a fence keeps a sheltered spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Eileen is a woman's first name, so a lady fits as an example.

clue.text: Perhaps ham or starter of piri-piri chicken?

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of piri-piri
a laying hen is a layer

explanation.surface: A menu choice: ham, or perhaps a starter of spicy chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' and 'chicken' look like the same menu, but ham is an overacting actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a bad actor, and an actor is an example of someone who plays a part.
